articles.title: Deploying OMP on Firebase Hosting in 4 Steps
articles.description: The whole site is static files — here is exactly how to put it on Firebase Hosting, with the security headers already configured for you.
articles.body:
Why this is easy

OMP has no server code, no database and no build-time secrets. Everything a visitor needs is plain HTML, CSS, JS and JSON in this repository — which is exactly what Firebase Hosting serves. Even the Articles feed is a static JSON file rendered in the browser.

The 4 steps

  1. Install the CLI and log in: npm install -g firebase-tools then firebase login.
  2. Create a project in the Firebase console, then run firebase init hosting in the repo. The included firebase.json already points the public directory at the repo root and ships recommended security headers.
  3. Preview locally first: firebase serve or firebase emulators:start.
  4. Ship it: firebase deploy --only hosting. Done — the site is live on your web.app domain with HTTPS.

Publishing new articles later

Write in the browser-based Article Manager, export articles.json, place it at content/articles.json, and redeploy (or push to a connected Git repo for automatic deploys). No servers touched, ever.

Free-tier friendly: static hosting of this size fits comfortably within Firebase's no-cost Spark limits for typical traffic.
